claims.text: The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase BCC high-entropy alloy.
The WTaTiVZr alloy possesses inherent chemical heterogeneity.
Chemical complexity in WTaTiVZr induces local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions lower the effective Peierls barrier for dislocation motion in WTaTiVZr.
The reduced effective Peierls barrier enhances dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr at high temperature.
The proposed lattice-distortion effect enhances cross-slip and dynamic recovery at high temperature.
Enhanced dislocation mobility and dynamic recovery produce distributed, transient dislocation substructures such as dislocation cells and slip bands.
Dynamic recovery prevents dislocation pile-up and promotes uniform plastic deformation in the WTaTiVZr alloy.
Distributed dislocation substructures blunt crack tips and delay catastrophic crack propagation.
Pure tungsten has a more uniform lattice than the chemically complex WTaTiVZr alloy.
Under the stated high-temperature loading, pure tungsten has limited dislocation mobility and initiates cracks earlier than WTaTiVZr.
At approximately 1200–1500°C under otherwise identical loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit significantly greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
At approximately 1200–1500°C under otherwise identical loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit significantly greater toughness than pure tungsten.
Compared with pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr will show a more uniform strain distribution and delayed crack propagation.
Pure tungsten will show limited ductility and earlier brittle-failure features relative to WTaTiVZr under the controlled comparison.
The proposed mechanism applies at approximately 1200–1500°C and moderate strain rates relevant to plasma-facing-component service.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at room temperature or at extremely high strain rates because other deformation mechanisms could dominate.
Matched high-temperature tensile testing with TEM or EBSD and fractography can distinguish the proposed dislocation-mediated mechanism from pure-tungsten behavior.
